title: Decomposing Predictive Roles of Semantic and Collaborative Information for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation needs to incorporate item textual semantics alongside interaction-based collaborative signals.

gap.claim: Existing methods often entangle semantic and collaborative predictive signals without explicitly modeling their distinct contributions to next-item prediction.

contributions.claim: The paper decomposes next-item predictive information into shared, semantic-unique, and collaborative-unique information.
RIDRec is a role-aware sequential recommendation framework that separately learns three role-specialized representations through alignment and separation constraints.
RIDRec adaptively fuses the role-specialized representations according to their relevance to the current user context.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe RIDRec as a novel role-aware sequential recommendation framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four public benchmarks reportedly show significant improvements over various existing sequential recommendation methods.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation benefits from combining textual semantics with collaborative signals.
Existing approaches entangle signals with different predictive roles.
The paper introduces an information-theoretic decomposition of predictive information into three components.
RIDRec learns role-specialized representations and adaptively fuses them for user-context prediction.
The authors report improvements across four public benchmarks and provide code.

source_observation.claim: Predictive information from different sources may have shared and source-specific roles.

interpretation.claim: Separating shared and source-specific information can clarify how heterogeneous signals contribute to prediction.

application.claim: For multimodal or multi-source prediction, model shared and source-specific roles separately before fusion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition is beneficial outside sequential recommendation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four benchmarks, baselines, metrics, or numerical improvement sizes.
The abstract does not describe the information-theoretic formulation, alignment constraints, or separation constraints in detail.
The abstract does not provide ablation results or independent verification of the reported effectiveness.
